title: The Cartographer's Sister
premise: A mapmaker receives an unsigned map drawn in her lost sister's hand.

storyBible.logline: Three years after her sister vanished, a mapmaker in a city of guarded borders receives a map in her sister's hand that leads somewhere no map is allowed to go.
storyBible.theme: What we owe the people who are no longer looked for.
storyBible.tone: Quiet, close to Mira, with dread kept under the surface.
storyBible.characters:
Mira Tallow: a junior mapmaker in the Bureau of the March. Careful, stubborn, the only one still looking for her sister.
Lysa Tallow: Mira's older sister, a gifted surveyor who disappeared three years ago while charting the old border.
Kael Varro: Mira's oldest friend, now a warden sworn to the Governor.
Governor Voss: decides what the official maps may show.
storyBible.relationships:
Mira and Kael grew up together; his oath to the Governor now stands between them.
Voss once employed Lysa and wants every map of the old border destroyed.
storyBible.worldview: The March is a frontier province where maps are law: a road that is not on an official map does not, legally, exist.
storyBible.rules:
A map drawn for oneself always misleads its maker, so mapmakers must rely on maps drawn by others.
Only the Bureau may issue maps of the border.
storyBible.keyEvents:
Three years ago: Lysa vanishes on the old border.
Chapter 1: Mira receives the unsigned map.
Chapter 2: Mira reaches the ferry at Low Ford; Kael arrives with a warrant.
storyBible.foreshadowing: A small mark on the map's corner, the sign Lysa used as a child, is planted in Chapter 1.

chapters.title: The Unsigned Map
chapters.content:
The parcel came on a Tuesday, which was the day the Bureau sent its worst errands to the junior desks. Mira Tallow signed for it without looking at the sender, because there was no sender.

Inside lay a single sheet, folded in eighths the way surveyors fold field copies, so the creases would not fall across a road. She knew before she had opened it fully. Some people recognise a voice in a crowded room. Mira recognised a pen.

The coastline was drawn in quick, unbroken strokes. The contour lines leaned slightly left, as if the hand that made them had been in a hurry to get somewhere else. In the corner, small enough to be mistaken for a blot, was a mark like a closed eye.

Lysa had drawn that eye on every map she ever made, from the age of nine. Lysa had been gone for three years.

Mira turned the sheet over. Nothing. She held it to the window, and the light came through a place where no town was marked, only a road: thin, deliberate, running north past the old border, where the Bureau's maps showed nothing at all.

She folded it in eighths again and put it inside her coat, against her ribs, where it could not be lost and could not be seen.

chapters.title: The Ferry
chapters.content:
The ferry had no bell. Travellers stood on the bank and waited to be seen, and Mira had been waiting since before the light. Her satchel held three maps she had not drawn and one she could not read.

She did not hear him come down the path. She knew him by the way the ferryman looked past her shoulder and then, carefully, at nothing.

"You should have gone farther," Kael said.

He had the warrant in his hand, folded once, the seal unbroken. He had not opened it. He did not need to.

"Read it to me, then," she said.

He looked at the paper for a long moment, and then at the river.
